questions.stem: A chronic smoker with history of COPD, presented with the following ABG findings - pH -7.2, Co2-60 mmHg, O2- 20 mmHg, HCO3-25. What is the diagnosis based on these finding?
questions.solutionHtml:
Respiratory acidosis, uncompensated
  • pH: Acidic (pH 7.2 indicates acidemia).
  • CO2: Increased (60 mmHg indicates hypercapnia).
  • O2: Decreased (20 mmHg indicates severe hypoxemia).
  • HCO3: Normal (25 mmol/L within the normal range).
  • These findings suggest primary respiratory acidosis due to high CO2 levels causing a decrease in pH. The kidneys haven't had enough time to compensate by increasing bicarbonate levels (HCO3), indicating an uncompensated state.

questions.stem: The upstroke of action potential (phase 0) in the sinoatrial node is due to:

options.label: A
options.text: Sodium influx via voltage gated sodium channels

options.label: D
options.text: Influx of both sodium and calcium

questions.solutionHtml:
Calcium currents only

Calcium currents only:

  • This is the correct option. The upstroke in the SA node is indeed due to calcium influx through L-type calcium channels during phase 0.
  • Stage 4 – pre potential phase. Ca2+ influx, If causing Na+ influx & decrease in K+ efflux
  • Stage 0 – depolarization phase
  • Ca2+ influx through L-type channels.
  • Stage 3 – repolarization phase
  • Due to K+ efflux

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is responsible for the phase marked C to D in the given nerve action potential?
questions.solutionHtml:
K+ efflux
  • Given is the resting membrane potential.

Phases of RMP:

  • Local potential change – due to slow influx of Na+
  • Depolarization – due to opening of voltage gated Na+ channels
  • Repolarization (C to D) – due to K+ efflux
  • Hyperpolarization (after D) – due to continuous K+ influx


Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, GK Pal – First Edition, Page No. 355

questions.stem: Which out of the following is the mechanism of cough?
questions.solutionHtml:
Expiration against closed glottis

Cough is an airway defensive reflex consisting of following stages –

  • Deep inspiration
  • Closure of glottis
  • Expiration against closed glottis
  • Sudden opening of glottis


Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, GK Pal – 1st Edition, Page No. 944

questions.stem: On neurologic examination, a patient is not able to identify an object but is able to recognize the object from its texture, color and pattern. Which of the following is likely to have been affected?
questions.solutionHtml:
Inferior Temporal lobe
  • Visual Deficits due to Inferior Temporal Lobe Lesion

Lesion Location:

  • Inferior Temporal Lobe: Results in deficits in visual discrimination learning.

Learning Impairments:

  • New Tasks: Difficulty in learning new visual discrimination tasks.
  • Previously Learned Tasks: Impaired memory for previously learned visual discrimination tasks.
  • Visual Perception vs. Visual Memory:

Perception Less Affected:

  • Visual perception is generally less affected.

Memory Disturbance:

  • Significant disturbance in visual memory.

questions.stem: Which of the following sodium transporters are present maximally in the early part of the PCT?Na k ATPase pumpNa H exchanger Na glucose cotransporterNa HCO3 cotransporterSelect the correct answer from the given below code:
questions.solutionHtml:
2, 3
  • Na-H exchanger & Na glucose co-transporter are present in the PCT.

Na K ATPase pump:

  • Location in PCT: Present in the basolateral membrane.
  • Function: Actively transports sodium out of the cell into the interstitial fluid, creating a sodium concentration gradient.

Na H exchanger:

  • Location in PCT: Present in the apical membrane.
  • Function: Exchanges sodium from the tubular fluid for hydrogen ions in the cell, helping to maintain intracellular pH.

Na glucose cotransporter:

  • Location in PCT: Present in the apical membrane.
  • Function: Couples the transport of sodium and glucose into the epithelial cell. It plays a crucial role in glucose reabsorption.

Na HCO3 cotransporter:

  • Location in PCT: Present in the apical membrane.
  • Function: Involved in the reabsorption of bicarbonate along with sodium.

 Summary:

  • Na H exchanger and Na glucose cotransporter are maximally present in the early part of the proximal convoluted tubule.

questions.stem: H+ secretion does not increase on Pentagastrin injection in which of the following conditions?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pernicious anemia

Pernicious Anemia:

  • Pernicious anemia is characterized by a deficiency of intrinsic factor, leading to impaired absorption of vitamin B12. Vitamin B12 deficiency can result in atrophic gastritis, which, in turn, can lead to reduced or absent parietal cells.
  • Without functional parietal cells, there's a diminished response to gastrin, and pentagastrin injection may not cause a significant increase in H+ secretion.
  • Pernicious Anemia is the correct answer because the intrinsic factor deficiency associated with pernicious anemia can lead to atrophic gastritis and a reduced response to pentagastrin.


Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, GK Pal – 1st Edition, Page No. 353

questions.stem: Motor supply of the muscle spindle is by which of the following?

A gamma
  • A gamma is the efferent neuron for a muscle3

questions.stem: Incorrect about baroreceptors present in the carotid sinus?

options.label: A
options.text: Located in the thick muscular layer of artery

options.label: C
options.text: Afferent fibers pass through the branch of glossopharyngeal nerve

options.label: D
options.text: They are sensitive to the changes in arterial blood pressure

questions.answerText: Located in the thick muscular layer of artery
questions.solutionHtml:
Located in the thick muscular layer of artery
  • Located in the thick muscular layer of the artery:
  • Baroreceptors are not located in the thick muscular layer (tunica media) of the artery. Instead, they are situated in the tunica adventitia, which is the outer layer of the arterial wall.
  • The incorrect statement is A. Located in the thick muscular layer of the artery. Baroreceptors are found in the tunica adventitia, and their primary function is to sense changes in blood pressure as stretch receptors.


Comprehensive Textbook of Medical Physiology, GK Pal – 1st Edition, Page No. 798
